newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots close mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots close mostly up.

text.p: -- Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday, with turnover rising to 9.79 million lots from 5.48 million.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract surged to 9.85 percent from 3.18 percent last Friday and the seven-day contract edged up to 9.15 percent from 9.05 percent.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

Traders said the rates were on a technical rebound after dropping sharply last week on news the central bank cut interest rates for the second time this year. They expect rates to move in a narrow range in the next few days.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up, continuing a bull run from last week after the central bank cut interest rates, traders said.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell to 3.02 million lots from 5.69 million.
But the most active ten-year bond that matures in June 2006 ended lower at 123.99 yuan from 124.25 after surges last week.
Traders said the spot contracts still had room to rise in the next few days but the room would be limited because they had begun to encounter profit-taking pressure.
